Prealgebra · Lesson 8.4

Arithmetic with Roots

Solve this lesson →All lessons

In 8.3 you simplified a single root. Now you combine roots by multiplying, dividing, adding, and subtracting them, and every answer stays exact with no rounding. Adding uses the like-terms rule from 6.1, with the root in place of the variable.

Problem
Multiply 3×123​×12​. Use the product rule to combine under one radical, then evaluate. What whole number is the result?
Show a hint
  • Join the two roots into one using the product rule. 3×12=3×123​×12​=3×12​. Now multiply the numbers inside.
  • You have 3636​. Ask yourself what number times itself gives 3636. That number is your answer, with no radical left.
Show the full solution
Both numbers slide under one radical. 3×12=3×12=36=63​×12​=3×12​=36​=6​ Two irrational roots can multiply to a whole number, and that happens exactly when the product underneath is a perfect square.
Problem
Multiply 6×106​×10​. Combine into 6060​, then simplify. What whole number appears in front of the remaining root?
Show a hint
  • The product rule lets you join two roots into one. Multiply the numbers underneath, so 6×10=6×10=606​×10​=6×10​=60​. Now 6060 is not a perfect square, so you are not done, you are exactly where 8.3 begins.
  • Find the largest perfect square that divides 6060. The squares to test are 4,9,16,25,364,9,16,25,36, and 44 is the biggest that fits since 60=4×1560=4×15. Split the root and pull the perfect square out, so 60=4×1560​=4​×15​.
Show the full solution
The product rule joins the two roots. 6×10=6×10=606​×10​=6×10​=60​ Since 60=4×1560=4×15 and 44 is the largest perfect square dividing 6060, we get 60=4×15=21560​=4​×15​=215​, so the number in front is 22​. Joining the roots is only half the job. Whatever lands under the radical still needs simplifying the 8.3 way.
Problem
Multiply 43×2643​×26​. The coefficients multiply and the radicands multiply. After simplifying the result, what whole number is in front of 22​?
Show a hint
  • Handle the two pieces separately. The coefficients multiply, 4×24×2, and the radicands multiply, 3×6=183​×6​=18​. That gives you 818818​, which is not yet in simplest form.
  • Simplify 1818​ the 8.3 way by pulling out the largest perfect square. Since 18=9×218=9×2, you get 18=3218​=32​. Now that loose 33 folds into the 88 sitting out front.
Show the full solution
The coefficients multiply and the radicands multiply, so 4×2=84×2=8 and 3×6=183​×6​=18​, giving 818818​. Since 18=9×218=9×2, 18=3218​=32​, and that 33 folds into the 88 for 8×3=248×3=24. The simplest form is 242242​, so the whole number in front is 2424​. Simplify last. Stopping at 818818​ gives the right value in an unfinished form.
Key idea
Multiplying roots. To multiply two roots, put both numbers under a single radical, a×b=aba​×b​=ab​, then simplify the result as in 8.3 by pulling out any perfect square. The number in front of a root is its coefficient, as in 4343​. Multiply the coefficients together and the radicands together, so am×bn=(ab)mnam​×bn​=(ab)mn​. Simplify last, and move any perfect square you pull out from under the root into the coefficient. That is why 43×2643​×26​ becomes 242242​. A bare root has a coefficient of 11, just as a bare xx meant 1x1x in 6.1. When abab is itself a perfect square, no radical is left and the answer is a whole number, as in 3×27=81=93​×27​=81​=9.
Fun fact
A-series paper (A4, A3, etc.) has sides in ratio 2 12​1. Fold any sheet in half and the result has the same ratio, so A3 folded is A4. The reason is 1÷22=21÷22​​=2​.
Problem
Evaluate (52)2(52​)2. The coefficient squares to 2525 and 2×2=22​×2​=2. What whole number is the result?
Show a hint
  • Squaring is just multiplying the expression by itself, 52×5252​×52​. Group the coefficients together and the roots together.
  • The coefficients give 5×5=255×5=25, and 2×2=4=22​×2​=4​=2. The root undoes itself. Multiply the two whole numbers you are left with.
Show the full solution
Squaring means multiplying the expression by itself, so group the coefficients and the roots. The coefficients give 5×5=255×5=25, and 2×2=4=22​×2​=4​=2. (52)2=25×2=50(52​)2=25×2=50​ A root times itself returns the number underneath, so (kn)2=k2×n(kn​)2=k2×n is a whole number whenever kk and nn are.
Key idea
Squaring a root expression. Squaring undoes a square root, so aa​ times itself equals aa. Squaring kaka​ squares the coefficient and removes the radical from the number under it, giving (ka)2=k2×a(ka​)2=k2×a. So (52)2=25×2=50(52​)2=25×2=50. The result is a whole number whenever the radicand is a whole number.
Problem
Simplify 67+2767​+27​. Both terms carry 77​, so treat 77​ like a variable and add the coefficients. What whole number is in front of 77​?
Show a hint
  • Treat 77​ like the variable xx from 6.1. Both terms are "some number of 77​", so they are like radicals and you only combine the counts out front.
  • Add the coefficients the same way you did 6x+2x=8x6x+2x=8x. Here that is 6+26+2, and the 77​ stays exactly as it is.
Show the full solution
Both terms carry the same root, so add the coefficients and keep 77​. 67+27=(6+2)7=8767​+27​=(6+2)7​=87​ The whole number in front is 88​. This is 6x+2x=8x6x+2x=8x from 6.1 with 77​ standing in for the variable.
Problem
It is tempting but wrong to write 36+64=?10036​+64​=?100​. Test it directly instead. What is the actual value of 36+6436​+64​?
Show a hint
  • Take each root on its own first. What is 3636​, and what is 6464​? These are both perfect squares, so each one is a whole number.
  • Now just add those two whole numbers. Do NOT add 3636 and 6464 under one root, a root cannot reach across a plus sign like that.
Show the full solution
Take each root on its own. Since 6×6=366×6=36 and 8×8=648×8=64, 36+64=6+8=1436​+64​=6+8=14​ The tempting shortcut gives 36+64=100=1036+64​=100​=10, a different number, which shows a root does not carry across a plus sign.
Problem
Simplify 38−7238​−72​. First simplify each radical, then combine. What whole number does the expression equal?
Show a hint
  • Simplify each piece on its own before you subtract. For the first, 8=4×2=228​=4​×2​=22​, so 38=3×2238​=3×22​. For the second, 72=36×272=36×2, so 72=6272​=62​.
  • Now both terms are like radicals in 22​, so this is just collecting like terms the way you did in 6.1, with 22​ playing the role of the variable. Subtract the coefficients, 6−66−6.
Show the full solution
Simplify each radical first. Since 8=228​=22​, the first term is 3×22=623×22​=62​, and since 72=36×272=36×2, the second is 72=6272​=62​. 38−72=62−62=038​−72​=62​−62​=0​ Two radicals that look different can turn out equal, which is why every term gets simplified before you combine.
Key idea
Adding and subtracting roots. Two radicals with the same number under the root are called like radicals. Only like radicals can be combined, just as only like terms could be in 6.1, with the root in place of the variable. Keep the shared root and add or subtract the coefficients, so 67+27=8767​+27​=87​ just as 6x+2x=8x6x+2x=8x, and a bare 77​ is 1717​. Roots do not combine across a plus or minus sign, so a+b≠a+ba​+b​=a+b​. A counter-example shows it, since 36+64=1436​+64​=14 while 100=10100​=10. Simplify every term before checking whether radicals match, because 3838​ and 7272​ look unlike yet both equal 6262​, so their difference is 00.
Problem
Simplify 25277​252​​. Use the quotient rule to write it as 252÷7252÷7​, then evaluate. What whole number is the result?
Show a hint
  • Use the quotient rule to pull the two roots together. 25277​252​​ becomes 25277252​​, so the real work is just dividing 252252 by 77.
  • Work out 252÷7252÷7. It comes out even, and the result is a familiar perfect square. Take its root.
Show the full solution
The quotient rule puts the division under one radical. 2527=2527=36=67​252​​=7252​​=36​=6​ Neither 252252​ nor 77​ is a whole number by itself, yet the quotient is, because 252÷7252÷7 lands on a perfect square.
Problem
Simplify 25494925​​. Split the root across the fraction and evaluate each piece. Write your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Pull the single root apart into two roots, one over the other. The root of the whole fraction equals 254949​25​​, so now you just need each piece on its own.
  • Both 2525 and 4949 are perfect squares. Since 5×5=255×5=25 you get 25=525​=5, and since 7×7=497×7=49 you get 49=749​=7. Stack them as a fraction.
Show the full solution
The root splits across the fraction, and both pieces are perfect squares. 2549=2549=574925​​=49​25​​=75​ Since 55 and 77 share no common factor, that is already lowest terms, 5/75/7​. Squaring back checks it, since (57)2=2549(75​)2=4925​.
Problem
Find 0.640.64​ exactly. Rewrite as 6410010064​​, apply the quotient rule, and write the result as a decimal.
Show a hint
  • Rewrite the decimal as a fraction first. Two digits after the point means hundredths, so 0.64=641000.64=10064​, and the quotient rule says 64100=6410010064​​=100​64​​.
  • Both pieces are perfect squares, with 64=864​=8 and 100=10100​=10, so you get 810108​. Now write that fraction as a decimal.
Show the full solution
Two digits after the point means hundredths, so 0.64=641000.64=10064​. Now split the root across the fraction. 0.64=64100=810=0.80.64​=100​64​​=108​=0.8​ Squaring checks it, since 0.8×0.8=0.640.8×0.8=0.64.
Key idea
Dividing roots. A quotient of two roots is a single root of the quotient, ab=abb​a​​=ba​​. When that quotient is a perfect square, no radical is left, as in 2527=2527=36=67​252​​=7252​​=36​=6. The rule also works in the other direction, so the root of a fraction is the root of the numerator over the root of the denominator. That lets you take the root of a fraction or terminating decimal exactly, as in 2549=574925​​=75​.
Problem
Simplify all four terms of 12+50+63+812​+50​+63​+8​. After combining like radicals, how many distinct radical terms remain?
Show a hint
  • Simplify each root on its own first. Pull out the biggest perfect square from each radicand, so 12=2312​=23​, 50=5250​=52​, 63=3763​=37​, and 8=228​=22​.
  • Now sort by what sits under the root. The 22​ terms are like radicals and combine into one term, while 33​ and 77​ each appear only once. Count the different square-free numbers left under the roots.
Show the full solution
Pull the largest perfect square out of each radicand. That gives 12=2312​=23​, 50=5250​=52​, 63=3763​=37​, and 8=228​=22​. The two 22​ terms combine into 7272​, while 2323​ and 3737​ have no partner, so the sum is 72+23+37,72​+23​+37​, which is 33​ distinct radical terms. The count is just how many different square-free numbers are left under the roots, and you can only see that after simplifying.
Problem
Evaluate each piece, then combine. (25)2+72×2−1805(25​)2+72​×2​−5​180​​ What single whole number does this equal?
Show a hint
  • Handle each of the three pieces on its own before you combine. Squaring 2525​ squares both the 22 and the 55​. For the product use the rule that a×b=aba​×b​=ab​. For the quotient use ab=abb​a​​=ba​​.
  • Each piece turns into a whole number. (25)2=4×5(25​)2=4×5, then 72×2=14472​×2​=144​, then 1805=365​180​​=36​. Now you are just adding and subtracting three plain numbers.
Show the full solution
Take the three pieces one at a time. Squaring. (25)2=22×(5)2=4×5=20(25​)2=22×(5​)2=4×5=20. Multiplying. 72×2=144=1272​×2​=144​=12. Dividing. 1805=1805=36=65​180​​=5180​​=36​=6. Now it is plain arithmetic. 20+12−6=2620+12−6=26​ Each rule turned a radical into a whole number, so nothing irrational survived to the end.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Simplify 5×455​×45​. Combine under one radical and evaluate. What whole number is the result?
Show the solution
The product rule merges the two roots. 5×45=5×45=225=155​×45​=5×45​=225​=15​ Two roots that are irrational on their own can multiply to a whole number when the product inside is a perfect square.
Practice
Find the value of 2×322​×32​. What whole number does it equal?
Show the solution
Both numbers go under one root, so 2×32=642​×32​=64​, and 8×8=648×8=64, giving 88​. Neither root is a whole number by itself, but the product inside is a perfect square, so the radical clears.
Practice
Multiply 6×146​×14​ and simplify fully. The answer has the form (whole number)2121​. What whole number is in front?
Show the solution
The radicands multiply, so 6×14=846​×14​=84​. Since 84=4×2184=4×21 and 2121 has no perfect-square factor left, 84=4×21=22184​=4​×21​=221​, so the whole number in front is 22​. Combining is not the last step. The new radicand usually needs simplifying too.
Practice
Evaluate 32×5232​×52​. The roots multiply to a perfect square, so the result is a whole number. What is it?
Show the solution
The coefficients multiply and the roots multiply. That gives 3×5=153×5=15 and 2×2=4=22​×2​=4​=2, so the value is 15×2=3015×2=30​. A root times itself always returns the number underneath, which is what clears the radical here.
Practice
Multiply 23×5623​×56​ and simplify. The answer has the form (whole number)22​. What whole number is in front?
Show the solution
The coefficients give 2×5=102×5=10 and the radicands give 3×6=183​×6​=18​, so the product is 10181018​. Since 18=9×218=9×2, 18=3218​=32​, and 10×3=3010×3=30. The answer is 302302​, so the whole number in front is 3030​. Multiply first, simplify last.
Practice
Evaluate (45)2(45​)2. The coefficient squares and the root cancels. What whole number is the result?
Show the solution
Squaring hits both parts, so 4×4=164×4=16 and 5×5=55​×5​=5. That leaves 16×5=8016×5=80​. Squaring knkn​ always gives k2×nk2×n, with the radical gone.
Practice
Evaluate (63)2(63​)2. The coefficient squares and the root cancels. What whole number is the result?
Show the solution
Squaring hits both parts. The coefficients give 6×6=366×6=36, and 3×3=33​×3​=3. (63)2=36×3=108(63​)2=36×3=108​ A root times itself returns the number underneath, which is why the irrational part disappears completely.
Practice
Collect like radicals in 103−43+3103​−43​+3​. What whole number kk gives the combined term k3k3​?
Show the solution
All three terms carry 33​, so only the coefficients change. The bare 33​ counts as 1313​, and 10−4+1=710−4+1=7, giving 7373​, so k=7k=7​. Forgetting that a bare root has a coefficient of 11 is the usual slip here.
Practice
Evaluate 144+25144​+25​ by taking each root separately, then adding. What is the result?
Show the solution
Take each root on its own. Since 12×12=14412×12=144 and 5×5=255×5=25, the sum is 12+5=1712+5=17​. Adding under one root instead would give 169=13169​=13, a different number, which is why a root never crosses a plus sign.
Practice
Simplify 27+4827​+48​. Each hides a factor of 33​. After simplifying, combine into one term k3k3​. What is kk?
Show the solution
Since 27=9×327=9×3, 27=3327​=33​, and since 48=16×348=16×3, 48=4348​=43​. Both terms carry 33​ now, so add the coefficients, 3+4=73+4=7, giving 7373​ and k=7k=7​. Radicals that look unlike often match once each one is simplified.
Practice
Simplify 52−5052​−50​. First simplify 5050​, then subtract. What whole number does the expression equal?
Show the solution
Simplify the second radical first. Since 50=25×250=25×2, 50=25×2=5250​=25​×2​=52​, so 52−50=52−52=052​−50​=52​−52​=0​ Five of something minus five of the same thing is nothing, and the two terms only look different before you simplify.
Practice
Simplify 30033​300​​ using the quotient rule. What whole number is the result?
Show the solution
The quotient rule puts the division under one root. 3003=3003=100=103​300​​=3300​​=100​=10​ Neither root is a whole number alone, but the quotient inside is a perfect square, so the radical clears.
Practice
Evaluate 964649​​ using the quotient rule. Write your answer as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The root splits across the fraction. 964=964=38649​​=64​9​​=83​ Since 33 and 88 share no common factor, that is already lowest terms, 3/83/8​. Squaring back checks it, since (38)2=964(83​)2=649​.
Practice
Find 0.810.81​ exactly. Rewrite as 8110010081​​ and apply the quotient rule. What is the decimal value?
Show the solution
The 81 sits in the hundredths place, so 0.81=811000.81=10081​. Now split the root across the fraction. 0.81=81100=910=0.90.81​=100​81​​=109​=0.9​ Squaring checks it, since 0.9×0.9=0.810.9×0.9=0.81.
